newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean junta member Mendoza buried near Allende.
newsitem.headline: Chilean junta member Mendoza buried near Allende.

text.p: Former Chilean military junta member, Police Gen. Cesar Mendoza, was buried on Sunday a stone's throw from the tomb of socialist leader Salvador Allende whom he helped overthrow in a 1973 coup.

Mendoza, who died of cancer on Friday at the age of 79, was buried in Santiago's General Cemetery and eulogised by former president Gen. Augusto Pinochet for "contributing so much to the basic restoration of the country."
Mendoza was buried in the police mausoleum, less than 300 feet (100 metres) from the crypt of Allende, who was overthrown and committed suicide in the 1973 coup led by Pinochet.

Mendoza, who collaborated with Pinochet in the coup, was one of the four members of the military junta, which took power from Allende and stayed in power until 1990, although Mendoza left the junta in 1985.

Reactions to his death, only two weeks after the death of another junta member, Adm. Jose Toribio Merino, revealed again the sharp divisions in Chilean society over the legacy of Pinochet's 17-year-long rule.
"One has to say at a time like this ... that the junta members led a cruel and inhuman government which violated human rights," said Jorge Schaulsohn, leader of the centre-left Party for Democracy.
Centre-right congresswoman Maria Angelica Cristi on Saturday called Mendoza "a great patriot who did a lot for this nation."
Chilean rightists revere the original junta members as the country's saviours from Marxism.
